rules: Never use generic Inter for headings.
Use IBM Plex Sans for body text to guarantee maximum readability for medicine names, dosages (e.g., 500mg), and batch numbers.
Bill total amounts must use 'bill_amount' (text-5xl font-black) to be instantly scannable by pharmacist and customer.
Use Medical Blue strictly for the primary CTA (New Bill, Pay, Save).
Use 'status' colors exclusively for stock expiry/warnings (Red < 30 days, Amber < 90 days, Green > 90 days).
Never use complete transparent backgrounds for overlays. Use solid or heavily blurred surfaces.

layouts.global: Single column, mobile-first constraint. No horizontal scrolling outside of specific carousels. Full viewport height.
layouts.bottom_tab_nav: Fixed at bottom, h-16 or h-20, evenly distributed icons. Active state in Medical Blue, inactive in Slate 400.
layouts.billing_screen: Sticky search bar at top (always focused), scrollable cart list in middle, sticky total & 'Pay/Print' button at bottom (Thumb Zone).
layouts.safe_area: Ensure padding bottom accounts for mobile safe areas.

rules: Thumb Zone Design: All critical actions (Add to Bill, Pay, Confirm) must be placed in the bottom 30% of the screen.
Touch targets must be at least 48x48px (p-3 or p-4 equivalents) to ensure error-free tapping in a fast-paced environment.

buttons.primary: Pill-shaped (rounded-full) or large slightly rounded (rounded-xl), Medical Blue background, White text, font-semibold. Minimum height 56px.
buttons.secondary: Outline or Ghost, Slate 200 border, Slate 800 text.
buttons.fab: Floating Action Button. Bottom right or Center Bottom. Massive (64x64px), Medical Blue, heavy drop shadow.

inputs.search: Large height (56px), solid surface background (Slate 50), subtle border, sticky top, large clear text.
inputs.stepper: Large + / - touch targets flanking the quantity number. No tiny dropdowns.

cards.medicine_item: Flat background (White), 1px subtle border (border-slate-200), no heavy drop shadows. Sharp corner radius (rounded-lg).
cards.confidence_chip: Inline badge next to matched medicine name. Green/Success for exact match. Amber/Warning + 'Confirm?' text for uncertain match.

rules: Abandon generic card drop-shadows. Use flat, clean, bordered components for a high-density, utility-first look.
Feedback: Buttons must have immediate active/pressed states (e.g., scale down or darken) for instant physical feedback.

image_urls.description: Medication capsules representing specific drug formulations

rules: Use these imagery exclusively where an image is necessary (e.g., visual catalogue empty states, or onboarding backgrounds). Never use generic placeholders.

icons.usage: Use thick, legible icons. Size 24px default, 32px for main bottom tabs.
rules: Do NOT use emojis as icons.
Ensure color contrast for active vs inactive icons.
Micro-interactions ONLY. No slow page transitions.
Skeleton screens for loading states (especially inventory search) rather than generic spinners.
Instant feedback simulation (fast color change on press) for primary billing buttons.
All text must meet 4.5:1 contrast ratio against its background.
Rely on color AND text for status (e.g., don't just use red, use Red + text 'Expiring in 20 days').
All interactive elements MUST include a data-testid attribute (e.g., data-testid='new-bill-button').

instructions_to_main_agent: You are building a mobile web app UI (Expo React Native equivalent styled with Tailwind/Shadcn primitives).
Focus heavily on the 'Thumb Zone'. The 'New Bill' CTA and 'Pay' CTA must be massive and anchored to the bottom.
Do NOT build a cluttered dashboard. The Home screen is just quick tiles and today's urgent stats.
The billing search bar must be dominant at the top and auto-focused.
For the Confidence Chips on uncertain matches, use a distinct UI pattern (e.g., amber background with 'Tap to verify' text) right inline with the search result.
Always use the provided JSON palette and typography structure. No 'Inter' font for headings.
Apply data-testid universally to inputs, buttons, and actionable lists.
UNIVERSAL GUIDELINES FOR MAIN AGENT: You tend to converge toward generic outputs. Avoid 'AI slop'. Make this POS system feel like a high-end, rapid-fire operational tool.
Don't make generic centered layouts. Left-align text for readability, center-align only large CTAs.
Use flat, crisp borders instead of muddy drop shadows.
Every interaction needs a micro-animation (pressed state, hover state if on web).
For toast notifications (like printer failures or stock warnings), use `sonner`.
